analysis_rows.segment: WordPress blog owners, content teams managing multiple old articles
analysis_rows.positioning: Plugin-based solution for automatic stale content notifications with granular control
analysis_rows.key_facts: Allows setting custom stale period, notification message, color, and post type filtering. Can be disabled per post via Block Editor

analysis_rows.segment: WordPress blog owners wanting transparency on content freshness
analysis_rows.positioning: Plugin displaying last modified date instead of or alongside publish date
analysis_rows.key_facts: Shows modification date for all posts; time range limited to 30 days. Provides three blocks for manual insertion

analysis_rows.segment: Developers comfortable with PHP and theme editing
analysis_rows.positioning: Manual code implementation for maximum flexibility in stale content handling
analysis_rows.key_facts: Requires editing single.php template; uses PHP functions get_the_time(), get_the_modified_time(), human_time_diff()

analysis_rows.symptom: WordPress blogs have many old articles that become outdated, irrelevant, or wrong over time

analysis_rows.evidence: Article states: site may contain many old articles and you may not have enough resources to update them

analysis_rows.symptom: Old posts with outdated content continue to receive search traffic

analysis_rows.symptom: DX Out of Date plugin continues showing old post notification on updated posts
analysis_rows.cause: Plugin uses post publication date to determine age, not modification date
analysis_rows.evidence: Article states: plugin uses the post's publication date to determine age
analysis_rows.fix: Manually turn off notification in Expired Notifications tab after updating post

analysis_rows.symptom: WP LastModifiedInfo shows modification date on recent posts as well

analysis_rows.evidence: Article notes: show the last updated date for all posts, including the most recent posts
